topic: Roman concrete — why some ancient harbors still stand

beats.narration: Some Roman harbors have survived 2,000 years in seawater.
beats.image_prompt: ancient Roman concrete pier extending into blue Mediterranean water, weathered but intact, sunny day, no people

beats.narration: Romans mixed lime and volcanic ash. Seawater triggered a chemical reaction that strengthened the material over time.
beats.image_prompt: close-up of porous ancient concrete with crystals, scientific macro photography, textured surface, no people

beats.narration: Modern concrete often crumbles in decades under the same conditions.
beats.image_prompt: cracked modern concrete seawall versus intact ancient stone structure nearby, contrast composition, no people

beats.narration: Researchers are still studying Roman recipes to improve today's materials.
beats.image_prompt: archaeological ruins of a Roman port at sunset, golden light on stone, calm sea, cinematic, no people
